rounds.text: Chordia Food Products Ltd is exhibiting a powerful recent acceleration in its fundamentals that outpaces lagging market sentiment [E54, E55]. Compounded sales growth has surged by 19% over 3 years and reached 51% over the trailing twelve months, while compounded profit growth hit 63% over 3 years and 44 over the trailing twelve months [E16, E17, E20, E21]. Furthermore, recent screen data highlights explosive near-term momentum with sales up 96% YoY and net profit up 108% YoY [E61, E63]. This operational turnaround is supported by pristine financial health, characterized by an exceptionally low debt-to-equity ratio of 0.03x and a conservative borrowing profile [E38, E57]. Cash generation is equally robust, boasting a cash conversion ratio of 2.95x where operating cash flow of Rs 2.30 Cr fully backs reported profit and translates into Rs 2.14 Cr of free cash flow [E34, E35, E36]. Conceded: long-term metrics reflect historical weakness, including a 10-year compounded sales decline of 19% and low historical returns on equity [E14, E59].

Chordia Food Products Ltd carries a valuation and fundamental profile that the evidence strongly undermines. The stock trades at an expensive P/E of 36.2x [E1], yet its intrinsic value calculated via discounted cash flow sits at just Rs 30 per share compared to its market price of Rs 70 [E43], resulting in a severe -135.0% margin of safety [E44]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that today's price already demands an aggressive 16.5% earnings growth rate, which vastly exceeds the baseline 5.0% assumption [E45]. This rich pricing is paired with suppressed historical returns, featuring a 10-year and 5-year median return on equity of a meager 3% [E26, E27], while its current ROE of 5.0% [E13] and 3-year average ROE of 4.77% [E59] lag well behind broader sector benchmarks [E9]. Compounded historical growth metrics also paint a picture of long-term stagnation, evidenced by a 10-year compounded sales contraction of -19% [E14] and a 5-year sales decline of -43% [E15], alongside multi-year negative or flat share price returns [E22, E23, E24]. Conceded: [E16] and [E17] show strong recent 3-year and trailing twelve-month sales growth of 19% and 51% respectively, and [E20] and [E21] demonstrate robust recent profit growth of 63% and 44%.
